module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: BASEL Norms and NPA Management (Level 1: Foundation)
introduction: At this foundational level, we will understand the biggest headache of the banking sector—NPAs (Bad Loans)—and the international rules (BASEL Norms) designed to prevent banks from collapsing. For clerical and preliminary exams, the full forms and the 90-day rule are the most frequently asked questions.

core_concepts.title: What is an NPA (Non-Performing Asset)?
core_concepts.description: When a customer takes a loan and fails to pay the EMI (principal or interest) for 90 consecutive days, on the 91st day, the bank declares that loan as an NPA or a 'bad loan'. Simply put, any asset (loan) that stops generating income (interest) for the bank is an NPA.

core_concepts.title: What are BASEL Norms?
core_concepts.description: Basel is a city in Switzerland. To protect global banks from economic crises and bankruptcies, an international committee (BCBS) created a set of banking regulations. These rules are known as 'Basel Norms'. Their primary goal is to ensure that banks maintain enough Capital (buffer money) to absorb losses from bad loans.

core_concepts.title: NPA in Agricultural Loans
core_concepts.description:
The standard 90-day rule does NOT apply to farmers.
- Short Duration Crops: A loan becomes an NPA if the installment is unpaid for 2 crop seasons.
- Long Duration Crops: A loan becomes an NPA if the installment is unpaid for 1 crop season.

important_entities.name: BCBS (Basel Committee on Banking Supervision)
important_entities.key_fact: The supreme international body that formulates the Basel Norms.
important_entities.significance: Established in 1974 by the central bank governors of the Group of Ten (G-10) countries. Its objective is to enhance understanding of key supervisory issues and improve the quality of banking supervision worldwide. RBI is an active member of BCBS.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume that missing an EMI for 1 month (30 days) makes it an NPA. This is incorrect! From 1 to 89 days, the loan is only classified as 'Overdue' or an SMA (Special Mention Account). The 'NPA' tag is strictly applied only after 90 days of default.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam asks about the NPA timeline, recall 'No Paisa Available after 3 months (90 days)' to instantly mark the right option.

exam_strategy_tips: For preliminary exams (IBPS Clerk, SSC), strictly memorize the full form of NPA, BCBS, and the agricultural loan exception (2 crop seasons for short-duration crops). These are high-frequency questions.
